citation: Fry AC, Smith JC, Schilling BK (2003). Effect of knee position on hip and knee torques during the barbell squat. Journal of strength and conditioning research.
intervention: Two variations of parallel barbell squats with load equal to body weight: unrestricted (knees allowed to move past toes) vs restricted (wooden barrier preventing knees from moving past toes)
summary: This study compared knee and hip joint torques during barbell squats when forward knee displacement was restricted versus unrestricted. Restricting knee motion reduced knee torque but increased hip and low-back torque, suggesting a trade-off in joint loading.
key_findings: Restricting forward knee movement during the barbell squat reduced knee joint torque compared to unrestricted squatting.
Restricting forward knee movement increased hip joint torque compared to unrestricted squatting.
Differences in knee and hip torques between the two squat conditions were statistically significant (p < 0.05).
The authors concluded that appropriate joint loading during the squat may require the knees to move slightly past the toes.
limitations: Small sample of seven weight-trained men; acute single-session design with no long-term or performance outcomes; only abstract available, limiting full risk-of-bias assessment.
